column1: GDPR — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Binding EU law; protects individuals in the EU/EEA regardless of where the company is based; covers personal data (broad — any PII).

column1: HIPAA — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Binding US law; United States; covers protected health information (PHI).

column1: NIST AI RMF — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Voluntary US framework, US-originated but referenced globally; covers AI system risk across its lifecycle (a process, not a data type).

column1: EU AI Act — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Binding EU law; AI systems placed on the EU market or affecting people in the EU; covers AI systems themselves, tiered by risk.

column1: ISO/IEC 42001 — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Voluntary international standard, global — adoptable by any organization; covers AI management system (AIMS) processes.

column1: Algorithmic Accountability Act — type, scope, subject matter?
column2: Proposed (not yet binding) US legislation; United States; covers automated decision systems — would require algorithmic impact assessments.

column1: GDPR — encryption, audit logging, residency, human oversight requirements?
column2: Encryption: not explicit, Article 32 requires only "appropriate" measures. Audit: no explicit clause, accountability principle (Art. 5(2)). Residency: no blanket rule, but cross-border transfer limits push toward EU/EEA Regions. Human oversight: Article 22 — right to human review of solely-automated decisions with legal/significant effect.

column1: HIPAA — encryption, audit logging, residency, human oversight requirements?
column2: Encryption: "addressable" under the Security Rule — implement or document an equivalent. Audit: required — Security Rule mandates PHI access audit controls (45 CFR §164.312(b)). Residency: none — governs access/encryption of PHI, not location. Human oversight: not mandated by statute, expected operationally for clinical decisions.

column1: NIST AI RMF — encryption, audit logging, residency, human oversight requirements?
column2: Encryption: not prescribed, defers to controls like AWS KMS (Manage function). Audit: recommended (Govern/Measure) for an auditable trail, not required. Residency: not addressed — a process framework. Human oversight: recommended (Govern/Manage), not mandatory.

column1: EU AI Act — encryption, audit logging, residency, human oversight requirements?
column2: Encryption: not direct — addressed via high-risk "accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity" (Art. 15). Audit: required for high-risk systems — automatic record-keeping (Art. 12). Residency: not required — focuses on training/validation data governance (Art. 10). Human oversight: required for high-risk systems — Art. 14 mandates a human can intervene/halt.

column1: ISO/IEC 42001 — encryption, audit logging, residency, human oversight requirements?
column2: Encryption: not prescribed, org selects controls via its own AI risk assessment. Audit: required indirectly — certifiable AIMS needs monitoring/internal audit (Clause 9). Residency: not addressed — an organizational management-system standard. Human oversight: Annex A controls on human oversight, scoped to the org's own risk assessment.

column1: Binding vs. voluntary — which frameworks are which?
column2: Binding law: GDPR, HIPAA, EU AI Act. Voluntary: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001. Algorithmic Accountability Act is proposed, not yet binding — don't confuse "proposed" with "voluntary."

column1: Scenario: "PHI" appears in a scenario → which framework, regardless of region?
column2: HIPAA.

column1: Scenario: "risk tiers" for an AI system → which framework, not GDPR?
column2: EU AI Act.

column1: HIPAA — which AWS mechanism satisfies it?
column2: BAA via AWS Artifact + HIPAA-eligible services.

column1: GDPR — which AWS mechanism satisfies it?
column2: EU Region residency + AWS Artifact DPA.

column1: EU AI Act — which AWS mechanisms satisfy it?
column2: Guardrails + Model Cards + Audit Manager.

column1: NIST AI RMF — which AWS mechanisms satisfy it?
column2: Model Cards + Audit Manager + AWS Config.

column1: ISO/IEC 42001 — which AWS mechanisms satisfy it?
column2: AWS Artifact ISO certifications + Audit Manager.

column1: Encryption at rest for Bedrock/SageMaker — key mechanism?
column2: AWS KMS; AWS-managed keys (e.g. aws/s3) for convenience, or customer managed keys (CMKs) for key-policy control, rotation, and auditability.

column1: Encryption in transit for Bedrock/SageMaker API calls?
column2: TLS/HTTPS by default — no extra configuration.

column1: Every CMK Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey call is logged where?
column2: AWS CloudTrail — KMS manages the keys, CloudTrail logs their usage.

column1: What does SageMaker encrypt?
column2: Notebook storage, training/inference storage volumes, and inter-node traffic during distributed training.

column1: What does Bedrock encrypt, and what CMK support exists?
column2: Data at rest/in transit by default; supports CMKs for custom models and fine-tuning data.

column1: Data-encryption CMK vs. model-encryption CMK — same key or different?
column2: Two separate, independent CMKs — one for the training-data bucket (data confidentiality), one for the fine-tuned model artifact (IP protection); neither substitutes for the other.

column1: Differential privacy — is it encryption?
column2: No — noise injected during training (DP-SGD) bounds what a deployed model's outputs can reveal about a training record; complements, doesn't replace, KMS.

column1: Confused pair: AWS KMS vs. CloudTrail (encryption context)?
column2: Don't confuse KMS (manages keys) with CloudTrail (logs key usage) — a frequent distractor pairing.

column1: IAM policy scoping best practice for Bedrock/SageMaker?
column2: Scope to specific actions on specific resource ARNs — e.g., bedrock:InvokeModel on one model ARN, never bedrock:* on *.

column1: What does a SageMaker training job or Bedrock fine-tuning job assume to act on your behalf?
column2: An IAM execution role — never embed long-term access keys.

column1: Resource-based policy — what does it restrict, and examples?
column2: Restricts access independently of the caller's identity policy; e.g. an S3 bucket policy or a Bedrock model resource policy.

column1: IAM Access Analyzer — what does it continuously flag?
column2: Resource-based policies shared with a principal outside your account/organization.

column1: Insecure plugin design — mitigation?
column2: Scope the Lambda/action-group IAM role to least privilege; validate inputs (e.g., account ID) server-side rather than trusting model-supplied values.

column1: Excessive agency — mitigation?
column2: Scope an agent's execution role/action groups to only the narrow actions its task requires; require human approval before high-impact actions (delete, terminate, modify).

column1: Scenario: an AWS service needs to call another AWS service on your behalf → ?
column2: Attach an IAM role — not embedded access keys, not a * wildcard.

column1: Interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) — what does it do for Bedrock/SageMaker traffic?
column2: Keeps it entirely within the AWS network — no internet gateway, NAT gateway, or public IP required.

column1: Which services use a gateway VPC endpoint instead of an interface endpoint?
column2: Amazon S3 and DynamoDB — don't default to "interface" for every service.

column1: How do you restrict which principals can use a VPC endpoint?
column2: Attach a security group and a VPC endpoint policy.

column1: Scenario: "must never traverse the public internet" / "isolated or air-gapped VPC" → ?
column2: VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) — not a NAT gateway (still routes through the public internet), not a VPN (connects networks, not a VPC to an AWS service).

column1: How can a SageMaker-to-Bedrock fine-tuning pipeline avoid the public internet?
column2: Route the fine-tuning job through a PrivateLink VPC endpoint so training data never traverses the public internet.

column1: Incident response — Detect phase tools?
column2: AWS CloudTrail (who/what/when on InvokeModel, CreateTrainingJob, etc.), AWS Config (unencrypted/public resource drift), SageMaker Model Monitor/CloudWatch (drift, anomalous invocation volume), Guardrails intervention logs (blocked topics, filtered content).

column1: Incident response — Contain phase actions?
column2: Revoke/rotate the affected IAM role or CMK; disable or throttle the compromised endpoint (API Gateway usage plans, Service Quotas); tighten the resource-based policy an IAM Access Analyzer finding surfaced.

column1: Incident response — Eradicate phase actions?
column2: Roll back to a known-good dataset/model version via SageMaker Model Registry versioning (data poisoning, supply chain); patch the anonymization/validation code that let sensitive data or a poisoned example through; strip/quarantine the offending source document from the knowledge base (indirect prompt injection).

column1: Incident response — Recover phase actions?
column2: Redeploy the vetted model/dataset version; re-enable normal throttle limits; confirm Guardrails (content filters, denied topics, PII filters) are active on the restored endpoint.

column1: Incident response — Post-incident phase actions?
column2: Assemble evidence with AWS Audit Manager (built on CloudTrail + Config) for the compliance/risk record; update the IAM policy, KMS key policy, or Guardrails configuration that let the incident occur; log the root cause against the relevant threat category.

column1: Model drift — attack or degradation, and what's the response?
column2: Degradation, not an attack — its "incident response" is monitoring + scheduled retraining, not containment/eradication.

column1: Scenario: "Which service shows a bucket became public three days ago?"
column2: AWS Config (configuration history), not CloudTrail.

column1: Insecure output handling — what is it, and mitigation?
column2: An app trusts/acts on raw LLM output (e.g., passes it to SQL) without validation; mitigate by validating/sanitizing/parameterizing LLM output before use plus Guardrails output filtering.

column1: MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications — what are they?
column2: Industry frameworks, not AWS services, for reasoning about AI threat categories systematically — ATLAS is an adversary tactics/techniques knowledge base for AI systems; OWASP Top 10 is a prioritized LLM-specific risk checklist, incl. insecure output handling.

column1: Amazon Macie — role in AI security?
column2: Discovers/classifies sensitive data (PII/PHI) in S3; primary mitigation for indirect prompt injection (pre-ingestion scanning) and sensitive information disclosure.

column1: Titan Image Generator watermarking — how does it work?
column2: Embeds an invisible, always-on watermark on generated images; Bedrock's detection API confirms its presence later to prove an image is AI-generated (provenance watermarking).

column1: Post-incident root-cause logging — which threat categories?
column2: Data poisoning, prompt injection, insecure output handling, model inversion/extraction, DoS, supply chain, sensitive-info disclosure, insecure plugin design, excessive agency, overreliance.

column1: Bedrock — customer responsibility?
column2: IAM permissions, data sent to/from the model, Guardrail configuration, encryption key choices.

column1: Bedrock — AWS responsibility?
column2: Physical infrastructure, host OS/virtualization, FM hosting & patching.

column1: SageMaker — customer responsibility?
column2: IAM permissions, training data pipeline, custom training/inference containers & code, VPC config for jobs.

column1: SageMaker — AWS responsibility?
column2: Physical infrastructure, host OS/virtualization, underlying compute/storage infrastructure.

column1: Bedrock vs. SageMaker — which has the thinner customer slice?
column2: Bedrock — most responsibility is AWS-managed; SageMaker is a thicker customer slice, taking on more configuration/code.

column1: Multi-stage pipeline — stage 1 (SageMaker Processing) responsibility split?
column2: Customer: container image/code, IAM role scope, VPC config, enabling KMS encryption. AWS: physical infrastructure, host OS, patching the SageMaker platform.

column1: Multi-stage pipeline — stage 2 (Bedrock fine-tuning) responsibility split?
column2: Customer: IAM policy scope, choice of training data, PrivateLink usage. AWS: training compute infrastructure, foundation model weights.

column1: Multi-stage pipeline — stage 3 (Bedrock Provisioned Throughput serving) responsibility split?
column2: Customer: Guardrails configuration, invoke-access IAM policy, CloudTrail logging. AWS: serving infrastructure, host OS, multi-tenant isolation.

column1: Is the customer ever not responsible for their data/access configuration?
column2: No — the customer is always responsible for their data and access configuration, regardless of how managed the service is.

column1: Does the shared-responsibility split apply once per pipeline or per stage?
column2: Per stage, not once for the whole pipeline — a data leak traced to stage 1's anonymization code is the customer's fault even if stages 2-3 ran on fully-managed Bedrock infrastructure.

column1: CMK — definition?
column2: Customer managed key — a KMS key giving key-policy control, rotation, and auditability (vs. AWS-managed keys used for convenience).

column1: AWS KMS — role in AI security?
column2: Manages the encryption keys used to protect data and models at rest.

column1: AWS CloudTrail — role in AI security?
column2: Logs API activity, including CMK usage and service calls (who/what/when).

column1: AWS Config — role in AI security?
column2: Tracks configuration history/drift — e.g., when a resource became public or unencrypted.

column1: Interface VPC endpoint — definition?
column2: A PrivateLink-powered endpoint that keeps traffic to a service like Bedrock or SageMaker within the AWS network.

column1: Gateway VPC endpoint — definition?
column2: The VPC endpoint type used by Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, instead of an interface endpoint.

column1: IAM execution role — definition?
column2: A role an AWS service assumes to act on your behalf, instead of embedded long-term access keys.

column1: Resource-based policy — definition?
column2: A policy attached to a resource (e.g., S3 bucket, Bedrock model) that restricts access independently of the caller's identity policy.

column1: IAM Access Analyzer — definition?
column2: Continuously flags resource-based policies shared with a principal outside your account/organization.

column1: Amazon Macie — definition?
column2: A service that discovers and classifies sensitive data (PII/PHI) in S3.

column1: MITRE ATLAS — definition?
column2: An adversary tactics/techniques knowledge base for AI systems.

column1: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications — definition?
column2: A prioritized checklist of LLM-specific risks, including insecure output handling.

column1: Differential privacy (DP-SGD) — definition?
column2: Noise injected during training that bounds what a deployed model's outputs can reveal about a training record.

column1: Excessive agency — definition?
column2: A security threat where an agent's permissions/actions are broader than its task requires.

column1: Confused pair: "proposed" vs. "voluntary" — Algorithmic Accountability Act?
column2: It's proposed (not yet binding) legislation — not the same as a voluntary framework like NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001.

column1: Confused pair: AWS KMS vs. AWS CloudTrail?
column2: KMS manages the keys; CloudTrail logs key usage — don't swap the two.

column1: Confused pair: AWS Config vs. AWS CloudTrail for "became public 3 days ago"?
column2: AWS Config (configuration history) answers this, not CloudTrail.

column1: Confused pair: interface VPC endpoint vs. gateway VPC endpoint?
column2: Bedrock/SageMaker use interface endpoints (PrivateLink); S3 and DynamoDB use gateway endpoints instead.

column1: Confused pair: VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) vs. NAT gateway vs. VPN?
column2: VPC endpoint = traffic never touches the public internet; NAT gateway still routes through the public internet; VPN connects networks, not a VPC to an AWS service.

column1: Confused pair: model drift vs. security incident?
column2: Drift is degradation — respond with monitoring + scheduled retraining, not containment/eradication.

column1: Confused pair: HIPAA vs. EU AI Act scenario cues?
column2: PHI → HIPAA regardless of region; "risk tiers" for an AI system → EU AI Act, not GDPR.

column1: Confused pair: training-data CMK vs. fine-tuned-model CMK?
column2: Two separate, independent CMKs — one for the data bucket, one for the model artifact; neither substitutes for the other.

column1: Confused pair: differential privacy vs. encryption?
column2: DP-SGD bounds what model outputs can reveal about training data; it complements but doesn't replace KMS encryption.

column1: Confused pair: shared responsibility applied once vs. per stage?
column2: Applies per stage of a pipeline, not once for the whole thing — a leak at an unmanaged stage is the customer's fault even if other stages run on fully-managed infrastructure.

column1: Numeric trap: HIPAA's audit-control citation?
column2: 45 CFR §164.312(b) — the Security Rule provision mandating PHI access audit controls.

column1: Numeric trap: GDPR's human-review citation?
column2: Article 22 — right to human review of solely-automated decisions with legal/significant effect.

column1: Numeric trap: EU AI Act's record-keeping vs. human-oversight citations?
column2: Article 12 mandates automatic record-keeping for high-risk systems; Article 14 mandates a human can intervene/halt — don't swap the two article numbers.
